name: Why is my shower faucet leaking?

mainEntity.name: Why is my shower faucet leaking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shower faucet leaks commonly stem from worn-out internal components. Over time, rubber washers, O-rings, or cartridges can degrade, leading to water dripping from the spout or handles. Mineral deposits from hard water can also accumulate and damage these seals, causing a leaky faucet. Identifying the exact cause usually requires disassembling the faucet to inspect the parts. A steady drip can waste a significant amount of water and increase your utility bills, so timely repair is recommended.
acceptedAnswer.description: Shower faucet leaks are usually caused by worn-out rubber washers, O-rings, or cartridges inside the faucet. Mineral deposits can also contribute to component degradation.
